title: Timeboxed booster credits plus SQ-gated upgrade journey
creator: Amina Patel
description: Run an experiment that issues small, timeboxed 'booster' credits mid-trial to high-engagement users to extend initial product experience and surface a differentiated upgrade path for accounts that look enterprise-y. Variant arm includes an enterprise Security Questionnaire (SQ) gating step as a soft sales/contract filter for higher-touch conversions. Goal: increase paid conversion and early retention while measuring cost-per-conversion and SQ completion friction.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment scaffold deployed with A/B/C/control cohort allocation and server-side feature flag
Event instrumentation in analytics for trial_booster_offered, booster_redeemed, sq_started, sq_completed, upgrade_clicked, upgrade_completed
Dashboard with primary/secondary metrics and p-value calculations available before ramp
Legal and Security sign-off on SQ flow and data handling (PII minimization), stubbed for dark launch
Billing edge-cases and coupon handling tested end-to-end in staging (redeem, expiry, invoice behavior)
experiment_design: Population: new free-tier/trial accounts created in the last 45 days, excluding customers with existing enterprise contracts
Trigger: user crosses engagement threshold (>= 5 generation requests or >= 3 embedding calls within 48 hours) OR explicit product milestone (first streaming response > 1k tokens)

Arms: Control (no booster), Variant A (self-serve booster + CTA to billing page), Variant B (booster + fast-path contact form to sales), Variant C (booster + SQ-gated upgrade path for accounts with corporate email domains)
Booster size: initial test uses 2,000 token-equivalent credits with 7-day expiry (sensitivity test planned for 1,000 / 5,000 tokens and 3/14-day expiries)
Allocation: 10% control, 30% A, 30% B, 30% C; expected N for power > 10k trial starts over 6 weeks
Messaging variants: In-app banner, email nudge, console toast (A/B text variants to test urgency vs. value framing)
metrics: Primary: Paid conversion within 30 days (upgrade_completed aggregated by cohort)
Secondary: Booster redemption rate, time-to-first-upgrade-click after booster, SQ start rate, SQ completion rate, 30-day revenue per trial, 30-day retention of paying users
Cost metric: incremental cost (credits issued) per paid conversion and projected ARR payback period
Quality guardrail: % of booster-triggered requests that exceed acceptable latency SLO (to monitor load spikes)
instrumentation: Events to emit: trial_booster_offered {user_id, cohort, offer_ts, credits_amount, expiry_ts}
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal test): QA and engineering validate redemption flow and expiry behavior using test accounts (1 week)
Phase 1 (dark launch): 5% of trial population; enable logging and internal alerts, verify SQ gating redirects and sandbox SQ storage (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (ramp): if no blocking issues, increase to 60% of eligible population over 7 days, monitor conversion delta and system load
Phase 3 (full experiment): run remaining allocation for 6 weeks or until statistical significance thresholds met, then analyze
Post-experiment: decision points for permanent product change, iterate on credit size/expiry, or retire boosters
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Credits are gamed by bots or multi-accounting — Mitigation: require signal of genuine engagement (API key usage fingerprinting) and rate-limit booster eligibility
Risk: SQ adds friction and reduces conversion — Mitigation: only show SQ flow to accounts with corporate indicators and provide clear value prop + sales follow-up for partially completed SQs
Risk: Cost of issued credits exceeds LTV of converted users — Mitigation: conservative credit sizes for initial run and run cost-per-conversion simulation in staging
Risk: Backfill complexity in billing — Mitigation: billing/finance alignment and negative-path tests for refunds and coupon collisions
follow_ups: If booster arm shows uplift, run factorial test on credit size (1k / 2k / 5k) and expiry (3 / 7 / 14 days)
If SQ arm drops conversion by >5pp but increases ARR per conversion, prototype a hybrid flow: quick SQ-lite + auto-sales-reachout
Surface learnings to Dedicated and Private sales teams and create a templated SQ package for account executives
comments: 2026-02-20 Amina Patel: Created ticket. Initial hypothesis: small, timeboxed credits given during high-engagement windows will lower early churn and increase self-serve conversions. Including an SQ-gated path to capture enterprise leads without immediately forcing full sales outreach.

2026-02-26 Design review (Maya Chen): Suggested two copy variants — 'Try more on us' (value-focused) vs 'Extend your trial now' (urgency-focused). Also recommended adding tooltip explaining SQ tradeoffs for enterprise arm.

2026-03-03 Engineering sync (Luca Moreno): Feasibility OK. Raised edge-case where credits could stack with promotional coupons; agreed to block stacking for boosters and log collisions. Need 3 days of work for instrumentation and 2 days for billing tests.

2026-03-06 Security review (Diego Ramos): SQ data handling flagged. Must redact certain free-text fields and persist only answer enums in analytics. Security sign-off required before ramp; flagged as blocker for Phase 1 unless sandboxed SQ storage used.

2026-03-10 PM decision: Reduce initial booster amount from 3,000 to 2,000 tokens and set expiry to 7 days to reduce cost exposure. Keep SQ gating criteria conservative (company email + usage > threshold).
2026-03-12 Implementation note (Luca Moreno): Server-side flag and event hooks deployed to staging. PR link added. Ready for Phase 0 QA next week.
